detail.name: National Identity Management Commission
detail.summary: For NIN Pre-enrolment and NIN Verification
detail.about: The National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) established by the NIMC Act No. 23 of 2007, has the mandate to establish, own, operate, maintain and manage the National Identity Database in Nigeria, register persons covered by the Act, assign a Unique National Identification Number (NIN) and issue General Multi-Purpose Cards (GMPC) to those who are citizens of Nigeria as well as others legally residing within the country. The NIMC Act 2007 provides for the establishment of the NIMC, its functions, powers, establishment of the National Identity Database, assignment of the National Identification Number (NIN) as well as issuance of token General Multi-purpose cards. The Act also provides the Commission with powers to make regulations connected with its functions. The NIMC Act 2007 provides the repeal of the law that created the former Department of National Civic Registration (DNCR) and the transfer of its assets and liabilities to the NIMC.
detail.vision: To provide a digital primary identity for all citizens and legal residents making it a reference point for all
detail.mission: We regulate a reliable National Digital Identity for citizens and legal residents to affirm their identity.

services.name: NIMC (NIN Pre Enrollment)
services.summary: NIMC's NIN pre-enrollment service allows you to fill out your demographic information online, book an appointment, and then finalize your enrollment at an official center by having your biometrics (photograph, fingerprints, signature) captured and documents scanned to receive your National Identification Number (NIN). This initial online step helps streamline the mandatory process of obtaining your NIN, which is required for many services and transactions in Nigeria.
services.dependency: ["Availability of network. ","Availability of the NIMS Backend. "]

serviceSection.section_description:
Step 1: Applicant visits NIMC website to access the Pre-Enrolment Portal: https://penrol.nimc.gov.ng and the online Enrolment Form. 

Step 2: Applicant fills in the Enrolment Form online, prints out a summary sheet with a 2D Barcode and heads to any NIMC Enrolment Centre. 

Step 3: Applicant verifies and confirms the enrolment data on the system. 

Step 4: Applicant has his/her headshot photograph, fingerprints and signature captured by an enrolment officer 

Step 5: Applicant has his/her supporting documents scanned. 

Step 6: Applicant’s enrolment is acknowledged; two slips are generated and given to the applicant: (a) Transaction Slip (b) NIN Slip indicating completion of enrolment. 

OR 

Rather than filling in the online pre-enrolment form and printing out a summary sheet with the 2D barcode, an applicant can also download the Enrolment Form to print out and fill. 

To download your enrolment form online go to www.nimc.gov.ng. Fill all forms in block letters and proceed to the nearest enrolment Centre for biometrics capturing in order to obtain the National Identification Number (NIN). Note: you can also pick up an enrolment form at NIMC’S ERC.

detail.name: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
detail.about: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) was established by Decree No. 15 of 1993 as amended by Decree No. 19 of 1999 and now the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control Act Cap N1 Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (LFN) 2004 to regulate and control the manufacture, importation, exportation, distribution, advertisement, sale and use of Food, Drugs, Cosmetics, Medical Devices, Packaged Water, Chemicals and Detergents (collectively known as regulated products). The agency was officially established in October 1992. The NAFDAC’s organization consists of the Director General’s Office and twenty (20) Directorates executing the functions of the Agency: The Agency also has six (6) Zonal Offices as well as FCT and Lagos State Office, all headed by Directors.

detail.name: Federal Road Safety Corps
detail.about:
The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) is a Nigerian federal government agency established in February 1988 under Decree No. 45 of 1988, amended by Decree 35 of 1992, and codified as the FRSC Act Cap 141, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria. The FRSC (Establishment) Act 2007 further formalized its role as Nigeria’s lead agency for road safety administration and traffic management. Headquartered at No. 4 Maputo Street, Zone 3, Wuse, Abuja, the FRSC operates across all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory under the supervision of the Federal Ministry of Works and Housing. Its mandate includes:

  • Preventing and minimizing road traffic crashes on highways.
  • Clearing road obstructions to ensure smooth traffic flow.
  • Educating drivers and the public on road safety and proper highway use.
  • Issuing driver’s licenses and vehicle number plates.
  • Enforcing standardized highway traffic codes and speed limits.
  • Providing prompt rescue services and medical care to accident victims.
  • Conducting research on accident causes and implementing preventive measures.
  • Regulating safety devices (e.g., seat belts, helmets) and mobile phone use by motorists.
  • Collaborating with stakeholders to enhance road safety.
  • Enforcing traffic laws with powers to arrest and prosecute offenders.
detail.vision: To eradicate road traffic crashes and create a safe motoring environment in Nigeria, working towards achieving zero road traffic deaths through 100% dedication to safety initiatives and global best practices.
detail.mission:
The mission of the FRSC is to regulate, enforce, and coordinate all road traffic and safety management activities through:

  • Sustained public enlightenment campaigns to educate road users on traffic rules and safety measures.
  • Effective patrol operations to enforce compliance with traffic regulations.
  • Prompt rescue services to provide immediate assistance to accident victims.
  • Improved vehicle administration, including registration and roadworthiness checks.
  • Robust data management to inform policy and accident prevention strategies.
  • Promotion of stakeholder cooperation with government agencies, private organizations, and international partners to enhance road safety initiatives.

services.name: FRSC (New Driver's Licence Registeration)
services.summary: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) manages the registration for a new driver's license in Nigeria, a process that involves mandatory training at an accredited driving school, passing a driving test with the Vehicle Inspection Officer (VIO), paying the prescribed fees, completing an online application, and undergoing biometric data capture at a Driver's Licence Centre (DLC) to receive the physical license card.

serviceSection.section_description:
1. Complete the driver's license application form online 

2. Visit VIO for driving test 

3. Pay the license online or at the bank 

4. Confirm payment at state BIR office 

5. Proceed to the FRSC officer at the DLC for biometric data capture

6. Visit your DLC/MLA/VIO and present your application form or temporary card to pick up your original license card

Process of obtaining a new license : 

Applicants must be 18 years and above 

Applicants must have completed driving school.
Make complaints @frsc.gov.ng or FRSC toll free emergency number 122

services.name: FRSC (Renewal of Driver’s License)
services.summary: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) Driver's License Renewal service allows Nigerian citizens to legally extend the validity of their driver's licenses by applying online, making payment, undergoing biometric capture, and receiving a new license or a temporary permit. The process often begins with an online application followed by payment, and then a visit to a Driver's Licence Centre (DLC) for a driving test and biometric data capture.

serviceSection.section_description:
Step 1 

Apply online at www.nigeriadriverslicence.org or in person at a Driver's License Centre (DLC). Step 2 

Pay the license fee online or at the Bank. 

Step 3 

Present your application form to the Board of Internal Revenue (BIR) Officer and Vehicle Inspection Officer (VIO) at DLC for endorsement. 

Step 4 

Proceed to the Federal Road Safety Corps Officer at the DLC for biometric data capture. Step 5 

Obtain a temporary driver’s license valid for 60 days. 

Step 6 

Pick up the original driver’s license at the BIR Office after 60 days.

services.name: CAC (Company Registration)
services.summary: This service enables individuals and organizations to establish legally recognized limited liability or public companies under the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA). The process involves reserving a company name, preparing and submitting incorporation documents such as the Memorandum and Articles of Association, and obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation. It also supports post-registration updates like changes in directors, share capital, or company address, ensuring full compliance with Nigeria’s corporate regulations.

services.name: CAC (Incorporated Trustees)
services.summary: This service facilitates the incorporation of non-profit and charitable organizations, religious bodies, and community associations. It allows such entities to operate legally, own property, sue or be sued, and enjoy perpetual succession. The process includes name reservation, submission of trustee details, constitution, and objectives, followed by approval and issuance of a Certificate of Incorporation. Post-registration, trustees can make changes to their constitution or management structure while maintaining compliance with CAC standards.

serviceSection.section_description:

2. Submission of constitution, trustee details, and statement of purpose.

3. Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and official registration extract.

4. Post-registration services like change of trustees or constitution updates.

5. Annual return filing to maintain active legal status.
